citation: one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law
paraphrase: Jésus déclare solennellement que pas la moindre lettre ni le moindre trait de la loi ne disparaîtra avant que tout soit accompli, jusqu'à la fin du ciel et de la terre.
contexte: Dans le Sermon sur la montagne, Jésus affirme qu'il n'est pas venu abolir la loi mais l'accomplir, et souligne la permanence de chaque précepte.

citation: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women
paraphrase: Jésus déclare avec solennité qu'aucun homme né d'une femme n'est plus grand que Jean-Baptiste, mais que le plus petit dans le royaume des cieux est plus grand que lui.
contexte: Jésus parle à la foule au sujet de Jean-Baptiste, après avoir demandé ce qu'ils étaient allés voir au désert et avoir cité la prophétie de Malachie sur le messager qui prépare le chemin.

citation: Of a truth thou art the Son of God.
paraphrase: The men in the boat came to Jesus, worshipped him, and declared that he truly is the Son of God.
contexte: After Jesus walked on water and calmed the storm, those in the boat worshipped him, acknowledging him as the Son of God.

citation: Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.
paraphrase: Jésus confirme que, selon la vérité, Élie viendra d'abord pour rétablir toutes choses.
contexte: Après la transfiguration, Jésus répond à ses disciples qui demandent pourquoi les scribes disent qu'Élie doit venir premièrement.

citation: Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven.
paraphrase: Jesus tells his disciples that it is very difficult for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.
contexte: After a rich young man walked away sorrowful because Jesus told him to sell his possessions and follow him, Jesus turns to his disciples to teach about the difficulty of riches.

citation: Whether of them twain did the will of his father? They say unto him, The first. Jesus saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.
paraphrase: Jesus asks which of the two sons did the father's will; when they answer the first, he tells them that tax collectors and prostitutes are entering God's kingdom ahead of them.
contexte: After telling the parable of the two sons, Jesus asks the chief priests and elders which son did the father's will, and they answer the first.

citation: thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth
paraphrase: They sent their disciples with the Herodians to Jesus, saying, 'Teacher, we know you are truthful and teach God's way truthfully, and you show no partiality to anyone.'
contexte: The Pharisees, plotting to trap Jesus, send their disciples along with the Herodians to flatter Him with words about His truthfulness before asking a politically charged question.

citation: Verily I say unto you, I know you not.
paraphrase: The bridegroom replies to the foolish virgins, solemnly declaring that he does not know them.
contexte: The foolish virgins arrive after the wedding door has been shut and plead with the bridegroom to open it, but he refuses to acknowledge them.

citation: Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.
paraphrase: While they were eating, Jesus told them that one of them would betray him.
contexte: During the Last Supper, Jesus and his twelve disciples are eating the Passover meal.

citation: Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:
paraphrase: Jésus affirme que tous les péchés et blasphèmes des hommes peuvent être pardonnés, sauf le blasphème contre le Saint-Esprit.
contexte: Après avoir réfuté l'accusation selon laquelle il chasse les démons par Béelzébul et averti que le blasphème contre le Saint-Esprit est impardonnable, Jésus déclare que tous les autres péchés et blasphèmes peuvent être pardonnés.

citation: and told him all the truth.
paraphrase: The woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had been done in her, came and fell down before Jesus and told him the whole truth of what had happened.
contexte: After a woman with a bleeding disorder secretly touches Jesus' garment and is healed, Jesus looks around to identify who touched him, and the woman, afraid and trembling, comes forward.

citation: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.
paraphrase: Jesus solemnly teaches that no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they receive it with the humble, trusting attitude of a little child.
contexte: After the disciples rebuked those bringing young children to Jesus, He became displeased and declared that the kingdom of God belongs to such as these, then emphasized the necessity of receiving it like a little child.

citation: but teachest the way of God in truth
paraphrase: They flatter Jesus, acknowledging his truthfulness, impartiality, and faithful teaching of God's way, then ask whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar.
contexte: Opponents sent by the Pharisees and Herodians approach Jesus in the temple to entrap him with a question about paying tribute to Caesar.

citation: thou hast said the truth: for there is one God
paraphrase: Le scribe approuve Jésus en disant qu'il a dit la vérité, car il n'y a qu'un seul Dieu et aucun autre que lui.
contexte: Un scribe interroge Jésus sur le plus grand commandement, et après la réponse de Jésus, il reconnaît la vérité de ses paroles.

citation: And as they sat and did eat, Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, One of you which eateth with me shall betray me.
paraphrase: Jesus solemnly declares that one of his own disciples, who is eating with him, will betray him.
contexte: During the Last Supper, as Jesus and his disciples were eating, he reveals that one of them will betray him.

citation: Truly this man was the Son of God.
paraphrase: The centurion, seeing how Jesus cried out and gave up the ghost, declared that Jesus was truly the Son of God.
contexte: After Jesus cries out and dies, the temple veil is torn, and a centurion standing nearby witnesses these events.

citation: who will commit to your trust the true riches?
paraphrase: If you have not been trustworthy with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true spiritual riches?
contexte: Jesus teaches his disciples that faithfulness in small, earthly matters is a prerequisite for being entrusted with greater, spiritual responsibilities.

citation: but teachest the way of God truly:
paraphrase: They asked him, addressing him as Master, acknowledging that he speaks and teaches rightly, shows no partiality, and truly teaches the way of God.
contexte: The chief priests and scribes, fearing the people, sent spies who pretended to be just men to catch Jesus in his words and deliver him to the governor; these spies question him about paying tribute to Caesar.

citation: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:
paraphrase: Jesus observes that the poor widow has given more than all the others.
contexte: Jesus watches the rich and a poor widow putting gifts into the treasury, then comments on their offerings.

citation: Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilean.
paraphrase: About an hour later, another person insisted that Peter was definitely with Jesus, because he was a Galilean.
contexte: During Peter's threefold denial of Jesus, a third person confidently asserts that Peter was with Jesus.

citation: And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
paraphrase: Jésus assure au malfaiteur repentant qu'il sera avec lui au paradis ce jour même.
contexte: Alors que Jésus est crucifié entre deux malfaiteurs, l'un d'eux reconnaît sa justice et lui demande de se souvenir de lui dans son royaume.

citation: Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre;
paraphrase: Some women of our group astonished us by going early to the tomb.
contexte: Two disciples, walking to Emmaus, recount to Jesus the recent events in Jerusalem, including the report of the women who found the tomb empty.

citation: That was the true Light, which lighteth every man
paraphrase: The true Light, which gives light to every person coming into the world, was present.
contexte: After clarifying that John the Baptist was not the Light but came to bear witness of it, the narrative identifies Jesus as the true Light that enlightens every person.

citation: full of grace and truth.
paraphrase: The Word became flesh and lived among us; we saw his glory as the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.
contexte: After describing believers being born of God, the narrator declares that the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth.

citation: but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.
paraphrase: Moses gave the law, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
contexte: John the Baptist testifies that Jesus, though coming after him, is preferred before him, and that from Jesus's fullness believers have received grace upon grace.

citation: Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!
paraphrase: When Jesus sees Nathanael approaching, he remarks that here is a true Israelite, a man completely without deceit.
contexte: Philip has just brought Nathanael to Jesus, and as Nathanael approaches, Jesus speaks about his character.

citation: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open
paraphrase: Jesus tells Nathanael that he will see heaven opened and angels ascending and descending on the Son of man.
contexte: Jesus responds to Nathanael's confession of faith after being amazed that Jesus saw him under the fig tree.

citation: We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen
paraphrase: Jésus affirme que ses paroles reposent sur une connaissance directe et sur un témoignage de ce qu'il a vu, mais que ses interlocuteurs refusent ce témoignage.
contexte: Nicodème vient de demander comment ces choses peuvent être, et Jésus lui répond en l'interrogeant sur son rôle de maître en Israël.

citation: But he that doeth truth cometh to the light
paraphrase: Celui qui agit selon la vérité vient à la lumière, afin que ses œuvres soient vues comme accomplies en Dieu.
contexte: Jesus explique que la lumière est venue dans le monde, mais que ceux qui font le mal la fuient, tandis que ceux qui pratiquent la vérité viennent à la lumière.

citation: hath set to his seal that God is true
paraphrase: Whoever accepts Jesus's testimony confirms by this act that God is truthful.
contexte: John the Baptist testifies that Jesus comes from above and speaks what He has seen and heard, though few receive His testimony.

citation: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly.
paraphrase: Jesus tells the woman that she has had five husbands and that the man she is currently with is not her husband, confirming that she spoke truthfully.
contexte: Jesus is speaking with a Samaritan woman at a well, and after she admits she has no husband, he reveals his knowledge of her marital history.

citation: worship the Father in spirit and in truth
paraphrase: The time is now here when genuine worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such people to worship him.
contexte: Jesus is speaking with a Samaritan woman at a well, explaining that true worship is not tied to a particular location but is offered in spirit and truth.

citation: they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth
paraphrase: God is spirit, so those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.
contexte: Jesus is speaking with a Samaritan woman at a well, explaining that true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth.

citation: And herein is that saying true, One soweth, and another reapeth.
contexte: Jesus is teaching his disciples about the spiritual harvest, explaining that they will reap where others have labored.

citation: we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ
paraphrase: The Samaritans tell the woman that they now believe not because of her testimony, but because they have heard Jesus themselves and know that he is truly the Christ, the Savior of the world.
contexte: After Jesus stayed two days with the Samaritans, many believed because of his own word, and they told the woman that their faith now rested on firsthand hearing.

citation: If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.
contexte: Jesus continues his defense, explaining that his judgment is just because he seeks the Father's will, and that his own witness would not be true.

citation: the witness which he witnesseth of me is true
paraphrase: Jesus states that another bears witness about him, and he knows that this testimony is true.
contexte: Jesus explains that his judgment is just because he seeks the Father's will, and he speaks of another who bears witness of him.

citation: he bare witness unto the truth
paraphrase: You sent messengers to John, and he testified truthfully about me.
contexte: Jesus continues His defense before His critics, citing John the Baptist's testimony about Him as true witness.

citation: This is of a truth that prophet that should come into the world.
paraphrase: Après avoir vu le miracle de la multiplication des pains, les hommes déclarèrent que Jésus était vraiment le prophète promis qui devait venir dans le monde.
contexte: Après que Jésus a nourri cinq mille personnes avec cinq pains d'orge et deux poissons, les gens, ayant vu ce miracle, le reconnaissent comme le prophète attendu.

citation: my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.
paraphrase: Jesus tells the crowd that it was not Moses who gave them bread from heaven, but his Father who gives them the true bread from heaven.
contexte: The crowd asks Jesus for a sign after he fed them, citing the manna their fathers ate in the desert, so Jesus corrects them about the true bread from heaven.

citation: For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to a crowd in the synagogue at Capernaum, explaining that eating his flesh and drinking his blood are necessary for eternal life.

citation: the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him
paraphrase: Whoever speaks on his own seeks his own glory, but whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true and there is no unrighteousness in him.
contexte: Jesus is defending his teaching in the temple, explaining that his doctrine comes from God who sent him.

citation: he that sent me is true, whom ye know not
paraphrase: Jesus, teaching in the temple, declares that the people know him and his origin, but he has not come on his own authority; the one who sent him is true, yet they do not know him.
contexte: Jesus teaches in the temple during the Feast of Tabernacles, responding to the crowd's debate about whether he is the Christ and where he comes from.

citation: Of a truth this is the Prophet.
paraphrase: Beaucoup dans la foule, ayant entendu la déclaration de Jésus, affirmèrent avec certitude qu'il était le Prophète annoncé.
contexte: Après que Jésus a parlé de fleuves d'eau vive, la foule réagit diversement à ses paroles.

citation: thy record is not true
paraphrase: The Pharisees tell Jesus that His testimony about Himself is not true.
contexte: After Jesus declares Himself the light of the world, the Pharisees challenge the validity of His self-testimony.

citation: Jesus answered and said unto them, Though I bear record of myself, yet my record is true: for I know whence I came, and whither I go; but ye cannot tell whence I come, and whither I go.
paraphrase: Jesus tells the Pharisees that even though he testifies about himself, his testimony is true because he knows his origin and destination, unlike them.
contexte: The Pharisees have just challenged Jesus, claiming that his self-testimony is invalid because he bears record of himself.

citation: if I judge, my judgment is true: for I am not alone
paraphrase: Even when Jesus judges, his judgment is true because he is not alone; the Father who sent him is with him.
contexte: Jesus responds to the Pharisees who judge by fleshly standards, asserting that his judgment is true because he is not alone but with the Father who sent him.

citation: the testimony of two men is true
paraphrase: Jesus cites the law stating that the testimony of two men is considered true, setting up his point that both he and the Father testify on his behalf.
contexte: Jesus is responding to the Pharisees after they challenged his testimony, appealing to their law about the validity of two witnesses.

citation: he that sent me is true; and I speak to the world those things
paraphrase: Jesus says he has much to say and judge about his listeners, but the one who sent him is true, and he declares to the world only what he has heard from that sender.
contexte: Jesus responds to the Pharisees' question about his identity, affirming that the Father who sent him is true and that he speaks only what he has heard from him.

citation: If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed;
paraphrase: Jesus tells the Jews who believed in him that if they remain faithful to his teaching, they are truly his disciples.
contexte: Jesus speaks to Jews who had just believed on him, continuing his discourse about his relationship with the Father.

citation: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.
contexte: Jesus addresses Jews who had believed in him, urging them to continue in his word as true disciples, and promises that knowing the truth will bring freedom, which prompts their objection about never having been in bondage.

citation: a man that hath told you the truth, which I have heard of God
paraphrase: Jésus leur reproche de chercher à le tuer, lui qui leur a annoncé la vérité qu'il tient de Dieu, contrairement à ce qu'aurait fait Abraham.
contexte: Jésus répond aux Juifs qui se réclament d'Abraham comme père, leur reprochant de vouloir le tuer alors qu'il leur dit la vérité reçue de Dieu.

citation: abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him
paraphrase: Jesus tells his opponents that they belong to the devil and do his desires; the devil was a murderer from the start and did not remain in the truth because there is no truth in him, and when he lies he speaks his native language, being a liar and the father of lies.
contexte: Jesus confronts his hostile listeners, contrasting their claim to be children of God with their true parentage, the devil, who has no truth in him.

citation: And because I tell you the truth, ye believe me not.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to a hostile crowd, contrasting them with the truth and accusing them of being of their father the devil.

citation: And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me?
paraphrase: Jésus demande qui peut le convaincre de péché et, s'il dit la vérité, pourquoi ils ne le croient pas.
contexte: Jésus répond aux Juifs qui refusent de croire en lui, après leur avoir dit qu'ils sont du diable et qu'ils ne l'écoutent pas parce qu'ils ne sont pas de Dieu.

citation: all things that John spake of this man were true
paraphrase: Many people came to Jesus and said that although John performed no miracle, everything John said about Jesus was true.
contexte: After escaping from those who sought to arrest him, Jesus went beyond the Jordan to where John first baptized, and many came to him there.

citation: Verily, verily, I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.
paraphrase: Jesus, troubled in spirit, solemnly testifies that one of His disciples will betray Him.
contexte: After washing the disciples' feet and predicting His betrayal, Jesus is troubled in spirit and testifies that one of His disciples will betray Him.

citation: I am the way, the truth, and the life
paraphrase: Jesus tells Thomas that he himself is the way, the truth, and the life, and that no one comes to the Father except through him.
contexte: Thomas asks Jesus how the disciples can know the way to where he is going, prompting Jesus to declare himself the way, the truth, and the life.

citation: Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive
paraphrase: Jesus refers to the Holy Spirit as the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot accept because it neither sees nor knows him, but the disciples know him because he dwells with them and will be in them.
contexte: Jesus is comforting his disciples, promising them another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, who will abide with them forever.

citation: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to his disciples after Judas's departure, using the allegory of the vine to describe his relationship with them and the Father.

citation: even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father
paraphrase: Jesus promises that after his departure, the Comforter—the Spirit of truth—will be sent from the Father; this Spirit will bear witness about Jesus.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to his disciples about the coming of the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, who will testify of him.

citation: Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.
paraphrase: Jesus tells his disciples the truth that it is to their advantage that he goes away, because otherwise the Comforter will not come; but if he goes, he will send him.
contexte: Jesus addresses his disciples' sorrow over his imminent departure, explaining that his going away is necessary for the Comforter to come.

citation: the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth
paraphrase: When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all truth, speaking only what he hears and revealing future events.
contexte: Jesus is comforting his disciples, telling them that although he has more to say, they cannot bear it now, but the Spirit of truth will come and guide them.

citation: the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent
paraphrase: Eternal life consists in knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, whom God sent.
contexte: Jesus prays to the Father, asking to be glorified so that he may give eternal life to those given to him.

citation: I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me
paraphrase: Jésus affirme qu'il a transmis à ses disciples les paroles que le Père lui a données, que les disciples les ont reçues, qu'ils ont reconnu qu'il venait du Père et qu'ils ont cru que le Père l'a envoyé.
contexte: Jesus, priant pour ses disciples lors de la dernière Cène, déclare qu'il leur a transmis les paroles de Dieu et qu'ils ont cru à sa mission divine.

citation: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.
contexte: In his prayer to the Father, Jesus asks that his disciples be kept from evil and sanctified, since they are not of the world.

citation: And for their sakes I sanctify myself
paraphrase: Jesus consecrates himself for the disciples' benefit so that they may also be truly sanctified.
contexte: Jesus is praying to the Father for his disciples, asking that they be sanctified through the truth, and he offers himself for their sake.

citation: that I should bear witness unto the truth
paraphrase: Jesus affirms that he was born and came into the world to testify to the truth, and that everyone who belongs to the truth listens to his voice.
contexte: Pilate is interrogating Jesus about his kingship after Jesus has stated that his kingdom is not of this world.

citation: What is truth?
paraphrase: Pilate asks Jesus what truth is, then goes out to the Jews and declares he finds no fault in Jesus.
contexte: During Jesus' trial before Pilate, after Jesus says He came to bear witness to the truth, Pilate asks this question and then declares Jesus innocent.

citation: And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true
paraphrase: The eyewitness testifies to what he saw, and his testimony is true and trustworthy, so that you may believe.
contexte: After a soldier pierced Jesus' side, producing blood and water, the eyewitness affirms the truth of his testimony so that readers may believe.

citation: and we know that his testimony is true
paraphrase: This is the disciple who testifies and wrote these things, and we know his testimony is true.
contexte: After Jesus' conversation with Peter about the disciple whom He loved, the narrator identifies that disciple as the author of this testimony.

citation: Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
paraphrase: Pierre déclare qu'il comprend maintenant en toute vérité que Dieu ne fait pas de favoritisme entre les personnes.
contexte: Pierre se tient devant Corneille et les autres Gentils rassemblés dans sa maison, qui attendent d'entendre la parole de Dieu.

citation: wist not that it was true which was done by the angel
paraphrase: Peter followed the angel out of the prison but did not realize that what the angel was doing was real; he thought he was seeing a vision.
contexte: After the angel freed Peter from prison and told him to follow, Peter obeyed but was confused about whether the event was real or a vision.

citation: Now I know of a surety, that the Lord hath sent his angel
paraphrase: Peter, regaining awareness, affirms with certainty that the Lord truly sent His angel to rescue him from Herod and from all that the Jewish people expected.
contexte: After being miraculously freed from prison by an angel, Peter comes to his senses and realizes the reality of his deliverance.

citation: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
paraphrase: Paul nie être fou et déclare à Festus qu'il prononce des paroles de vérité et de bon sens.
contexte: Paul répond à Festus, qui l'a accusé de folie après son témoignage sur la résurrection du Christ.

citation: who hold the truth in unrighteousness
paraphrase: God's wrath is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth by their wickedness.
contexte: Paul has just declared the gospel as God's power for salvation and the revelation of God's righteousness by faith, and now contrasts this with God's wrath revealed against those who suppress the truth.

citation: Who changed the truth of God into a lie
paraphrase: They exchanged God's truth for a lie, worshiping and serving created things rather than the Creator, who is forever praised.
contexte: Paul describes humanity's descent into idolatry, where they exchanged God's glory for images and His truth for lies.

citation: the judgment of God is according to truth
paraphrase: Paul affirms that God's judgment against those who commit such sins is based on truth.
contexte: Paul addresses those who judge others while committing the same sins, warning them of God's truthful judgment.

citation: and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness
paraphrase: God will bring indignation and wrath upon those who are contentious, disobey the truth, and follow unrighteousness.
contexte: Paul explains that God will render to each person according to their deeds, contrasting those who persevere in good with those who are contentious and disobedient.

citation: the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law
paraphrase: Tu te considères comme un instructeur des ignorants et un enseignant des simples, parce que tu possèdes dans la loi l'apparence de la connaissance et de la vérité.
contexte: Paul s'adresse aux Juifs qui se vantent d'être guides des aveugles et instruits par la loi, tout en ne la mettant pas en pratique eux-mêmes.

citation: let God be true, but every man a liar
paraphrase: Paul rejects the idea that human unfaithfulness nullifies God's faithfulness, affirming that God is true and every person a liar, as Scripture says God is justified in His words and prevails when judged.
contexte: Paul is addressing whether Jewish unbelief nullifies God's faithfulness, arguing that God remains true despite human falsehood.

citation: For if the truth of God hath more abounded through my lie unto his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?
paraphrase: Paul asks: if God's truthfulness is magnified by my falsehood, why am I still condemned as a sinner? He rejects the slanderous charge that he encourages doing evil so that good may come.
contexte: Paul responds to a hypothetical objector who twists his teaching to suggest that lying is acceptable if it enhances God's glory.

citation: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not
paraphrase: Paul declares that he speaks truth in Christ, not lying, with his conscience confirming it through the Holy Spirit.
contexte: Paul is expressing his deep sorrow for his fellow Israelites, affirming his sincerity in Christ.

citation: Be not highminded, but fear:
paraphrase: C'est par l'incrédulité que les branches ont été retranchées, et toi tu tiens par la foi ; ne t'enorgueillis pas, mais crains.
contexte: Paul répond à l'objection d'un Gentil croyant qui pourrait se vanter d'avoir été greffé à la place des branches incrédules.

citation: For meat destroy not the work of God. All things indeed are pure; but it is evil for that man who eateth with offence.
paraphrase: Do not let your eating destroy God's work; all foods are pure, but it is wrong for someone to eat in a way that causes offense.
contexte: Paul exhorts believers to avoid causing others to stumble over matters of food and drink, emphasizing peace and mutual edification.

citation: Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God
paraphrase: Paul déclare que Jésus-Christ a servi les Juifs (les circoncis) pour démontrer la fidélité de Dieu à ses promesses faites aux patriarches.
contexte: Paul exhorte les chrétiens à s'accueillir mutuellement, comme le Christ les a accueillis, en expliquant que Jésus est devenu serviteur des circoncis pour manifester la vérité de Dieu.

citation: the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth
paraphrase: Paul calls believers to celebrate the Christian life not with the old leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
contexte: Paul urges the Corinthian church to purge out the old leaven of sin, since Christ our Passover has been sacrificed.

citation: but rejoiceth in the truth;
paraphrase: Love does not take pleasure in wrongdoing, but finds joy in the truth.
contexte: Paul continues his discourse on the nature of charity (love), describing its attributes in a series of contrasts.

citation: But as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay.
contexte: Paul defends his change of travel plans, insisting that his word to the Corinthians was not fickle but as reliable as God's truthfulness.

citation: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
paraphrase: Paul déclare avoir renoncé aux pratiques honteuses et à la tromperie, ne falsifiant pas la parole de Dieu, mais manifestant ouvertement la vérité pour convaincre la conscience de chaque homme devant Dieu.
contexte: Paul défend son ministère en affirmant qu'il a renoncé à la tromperie et manifeste la vérité devant Dieu.

citation: By the word of truth, by the power of God
paraphrase: Paul describes how he and his fellow workers commend themselves in every situation, including by speaking the word of truth, relying on God's power, and using righteousness as armor on both sides.
contexte: Paul lists the hardships and virtues that authenticate his ministry, contrasting outward dishonor with inward truth.

citation: as deceivers, and yet true;
paraphrase: Paul décrit son ministère comme marqué à la fois par la mauvaise et la bonne réputation, étant considéré comme trompeur tout en étant véritable.
contexte: Paul énumère les épreuves et les qualités qui authentifient son ministère, y compris les contrastes entre honneur et déshonneur, mauvaise et bonne réputation, en se présentant comme des imposteurs mais véridiques.

citation: For if I have boasted any thing to him of you, I am not ashamed; but as we spake all things to you in truth, even so our boasting, which I made before Titus, is found a truth.
paraphrase: Paul says that if he boasted to Titus about the Corinthians, he was not ashamed, because just as he had spoken everything to them in truth, so his boasting to Titus proved to be true.
contexte: Paul explains that his previous boasting about the Corinthian church to Titus was justified, bringing him comfort and joy.

citation: As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me
paraphrase: Paul affirms that the truth of Christ is in him, and boasts that no one will silence his boasting in Achaia.
contexte: Paul defends his ministry, explaining that he refused financial support from the Corinthians and will continue to do so, unlike false apostles.

citation: for I will say the truth
paraphrase: Paul says that even if he wanted to boast, he would not be foolish because he would speak the truth, but he refrains so that no one thinks more of him than what they see or hear.
contexte: Paul discusses his reluctance to boast about his revelations, preferring to speak truthfully while avoiding undue exaltation.

citation: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
contexte: Paul writes to the Corinthians about his apostolic authority, hoping they will do good and be made perfect.

citation: that the truth of the gospel might continue with you
paraphrase: Paul and his companions refused, even briefly, to submit to the false brethren, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with the Galatians.
contexte: Paul recounts how false brethren sought to spy out their liberty in Christ and bring them into bondage, but he refused to yield to them.

citation: they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel
paraphrase: When Paul saw that Peter and the other Jews were not acting consistently with the gospel's truth, he confronted Peter in front of everyone, asking why he, a Jew who lives like a Gentile, was forcing Gentiles to live like Jews.
contexte: Paul confronts Peter publicly in Antioch because Peter had withdrawn from eating with Gentiles after certain men came from James, causing others to follow his hypocrisy.

citation: Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?
contexte: Paul reminds the Galatians how they once received him warmly, and now asks if his truthful preaching has turned them against him.

citation: who did hinder you that ye should not obey the truth?
paraphrase: Paul asks why the Galatians, who started well, were stopped from obeying the truth.
contexte: Paul is writing to the Galatians to correct their turn from the true gospel to false teaching.

citation: ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation
paraphrase: En Christ, vous avez aussi mis votre confiance après avoir entendu la parole de vérité, l'Évangile de votre salut, et après avoir cru, vous avez été scellés du Saint-Esprit promis.
contexte: Paul explique aux Éphésiens que, après avoir entendu l'Évangile, ils ont cru et ont été scellés du Saint-Esprit.

citation: But speaking the truth in love
paraphrase: En disant la vérité avec amour, nous devons grandir en toutes choses en Christ, qui est le chef de l'Église.
contexte: Paul exhorte les croyants à ne plus être des enfants ballottés par toutes sortes de doctrines, mais à grandir en Christ en parlant la vérité dans l'amour.

citation: as the truth is in Jesus:
paraphrase: Si vous avez vraiment entendu le Christ et été instruits par lui, vous savez que la vérité se trouve en Jésus.
contexte: Paul contrast les païens endurcis avec les Éphésiens qui ont appris le Christ, les appelant à se dépouiller du vieil homme.

citation: which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness
paraphrase: Paul instructs believers to clothe themselves with the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.
contexte: Paul urges the Ephesians to abandon their old, corrupt way of life and embrace renewal in their minds, putting on the new man created in God's likeness.

citation: putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour
paraphrase: Rejetant le mensonge, que chacun dise la vérité à son prochain, car nous sommes membres les uns des autres.
contexte: Paul exhorte les croyants, renouvelés en esprit et ayant revêtu l'homme nouveau, à abandonner le mensonge dans leurs relations mutuelles.

citation: the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth
paraphrase: Le fruit de l'Esprit se manifeste dans toute bonté, justice et vérité.
contexte: Paul exhorte les croyants à marcher comme enfants de lumière, après avoir été ténèbres, et à discerner ce qui est agréable au Seigneur.

citation: having your loins girt about with truth
paraphrase: Tenez ferme, en ayant la vérité pour ceinture autour de vos reins, et la justice pour cuirasse.
contexte: Paul exhorte les croyants à revêtir l'armure de Dieu pour résister aux attaques spirituelles dans le combat contre les forces du mal.

citation: whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached
paraphrase: Paul se réjouit que, de toute manière, que ce soit par prétexte ou sincèrement, le Christ soit annoncé.
contexte: Certains prêchent le Christ par envie et rivalité, d'autres par amour, et Paul réagit à ces motivations opposées.

citation: whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest
paraphrase: Enfin, frères, pensez à tout ce qui est vrai, honorable, juste, pur, aimable et de bonne réputation, à tout ce qui est vertueux et mérite louange.
contexte: Paul conclut ses exhortations aux Philippiens en les appelant à fixer leurs pensées sur tout ce qui est vrai, honorable et digne de louange.

citation: the word of the truth of the gospel
paraphrase: Paul parle de l'espérance réservée au ciel pour les Colossiens, qu'ils ont déjà entendue dans la prédication de la vérité de l'Évangile.
contexte: Paul remercie Dieu pour la foi des Colossiens et l'amour qu'ils ont pour tous les saints, en raison de l'espérance qui leur est réservée dans les cieux et dont ils ont entendu parler dans l'Évangile.

citation: knew the grace of God in truth
paraphrase: L'Évangile, présent dans le monde entier, porte du fruit chez les Colossiens depuis qu'ils ont entendu parler de la grâce de Dieu et l'ont connue dans la vérité.
contexte: Paul continue sa prière de reconnaissance pour les Colossiens, qui ont entendu l'Évangile et en ont connu la vérité.

citation: but as it is in truth, the word of God
paraphrase: Paul remercie Dieu sans cesse parce que les Thessaloniciens, en recevant la parole de Dieu annoncée par lui, l'ont acceptée non comme une parole humaine, mais comme ce qu'elle est véritablement, la parole de Dieu, qui agit efficacement en ceux qui croient.
contexte: Paul remercie Dieu parce que les Thessaloniciens ont accueilli sa prédication non comme une parole humaine, mais comme la parole de Dieu.

citation: the love of the truth, that they might be saved
paraphrase: Those who are perishing are deceived by unrighteousness because they refused to love the truth that would have saved them.
contexte: Paul describes the coming of the Wicked one, whose deceptive signs and wonders lead to perdition those who reject the truth.

citation: who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.
paraphrase: Those who refuse to believe the truth and instead take pleasure in unrighteousness will face condemnation.
contexte: Paul warns that God will send strong delusion to those who reject the truth, so they may be condemned.

citation: through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth:
paraphrase: Nous devons toujours rendre grâce à Dieu pour vous, frères bien-aimés du Seigneur, parce que Dieu vous a choisis dès le commencement pour le salut, par l'œuvre sanctifiante de l'Esprit et par votre foi en la vérité.
contexte: Paul contrastes les croyants avec ceux qui périssent parce qu'ils ont refusé d'aimer la vérité, en rendant grâce pour l'élection des Thessaloniciens au salut.

citation: to come unto the knowledge of the truth
paraphrase: God our Savior desires that every person be saved and come to know the truth.
contexte: Paul urges prayers for all people, including rulers, because God our Savior wants everyone to be saved and to know the truth.

citation: I speak the truth in Christ, and lie not
paraphrase: Paul affirms that God appointed him as a preacher and apostle to the Gentiles, and he solemnly declares that he speaks the truth in Christ without lying, teaching them in faith and truth.
contexte: Paul explains his apostolic mission in light of the one God and mediator, Jesus Christ, who gave himself as a ransom for all.

citation: the pillar and ground of the truth.
paraphrase: Paul instructs Timothy on proper conduct in God's household, the church of the living God, which upholds and supports the truth.
contexte: Paul writes to Timothy, hoping to visit soon, but provides instructions in case he is delayed.

citation: Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.
paraphrase: Paul describes false teachers who forbid marriage and certain foods, yet God created these to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
contexte: Paul warns Timothy that in the latter times some will depart from the faith, following deceiving spirits and doctrines of demons, forbidding marriage and demanding abstinence from foods.

citation: Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God
paraphrase: La véritable veuve, abandonnée, place sa confiance en Dieu et persévère dans les supplications et les prières nuit et jour.
contexte: Paul donne des instructions à Timothée sur la manière d'honorer les veuves, en distinguant celles qui sont réellement dans le besoin et mettent leur confiance en Dieu.

citation: destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness
paraphrase: Paul describes people with corrupt minds who have abandoned the truth, believing that godliness is a way to get rich, and he instructs Timothy to stay away from such people.
contexte: Paul warns Timothy about false teachers who are proud, stir up strife, and think that godliness is a means of financial gain.

citation: Laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come
paraphrase: En accumulant un bon fondement pour l'avenir, ils pourront saisir la vie éternelle.
contexte: Paul conclut ses instructions à Timothée sur la manière dont les riches doivent utiliser leurs biens pour s'assurer un trésor éternel.

citation: rightly dividing the word of truth
paraphrase: Be diligent to present yourself approved to God as an unashamed worker who correctly handles the word of truth.
contexte: Paul exhorts Timothy to faithful, approved service and to avoid fruitless word battles that subvert hearers.

citation: Who concerning the truth have erred
paraphrase: These individuals have strayed from the truth, claiming the resurrection has already happened, and have undermined the faith of some.
contexte: Paul warns Timothy about false teachers like Hymenaeus and Philetus, whose misleading words spread like gangrene and destroy faith.

citation: repentance to the acknowledging of the truth;
paraphrase: Correct opponents with gentleness, hoping God may grant them repentance leading to knowledge of the truth.
contexte: Paul exhorts Timothy to avoid foolish disputations and to gently instruct those who oppose the faith, hoping God grants them repentance.

citation: never able to come to the knowledge of the truth
paraphrase: They are always learning but never able to arrive at the knowledge of the truth.
contexte: Paul warns Timothy about false teachers who have an outward form of godliness but deny its power, creeping into homes and leading people astray.

citation: so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds
paraphrase: Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, these false teachers also oppose the truth; they have corrupted minds and are rejected regarding the faith.
contexte: Paul warns Timothy about false teachers who, like Jannes and Jambres opposing Moses, resist the truth and corrupt the faith.

citation: turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables
paraphrase: Paul warns Timothy that people will reject the truth and instead turn to myths.
contexte: Paul charges Timothy to preach the word faithfully because a time is coming when people will reject sound doctrine and turn to myths.

citation: the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness
paraphrase: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, writes to further the faith of God's chosen people and their knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness.
contexte: Paul opens his letter to Titus by identifying himself as a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, sent to promote the faith of God's elect and their knowledge of the truth.

citation: Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught
paraphrase: L'évêque doit s'attacher fermement à la parole fidèle qu'il a reçue, afin de pouvoir, par un enseignement sain, exhorter et convaincre ceux qui s'opposent.
contexte: Paul décrit les qualifications d'un évêque, qui doit être irréprochable et attaché à la parole fidèle pour enseigner et réfuter les contradicteurs.

citation: This witness is true.
paraphrase: Paul affirms that the testimony about the Cretans is true, and therefore instructs Titus to rebuke them sharply so they may become sound in the faith.
contexte: Paul is instructing Titus about the corrupt teachers in Crete, quoting a Cretan prophet's description of his own people as liars, and affirming that this testimony is true.

citation: Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.
paraphrase: Paul warns against paying attention to Jewish myths and human rules that lead people away from the truth.
contexte: Paul instructs Titus to rebuke the Cretans sharply so they may be sound in the faith and not pay attention to Jewish fables and human commandments.

citation: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
paraphrase: Christ serves as a minister in the true sanctuary and tabernacle, which the Lord established, not humans.
contexte: Paul continues his discussion of Christ as our high priest, emphasizing that He serves in the true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man.

citation: but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:
paraphrase: Christ did not enter a man-made sanctuary that merely copies the true one, but he entered heaven itself to appear before God on our behalf.
contexte: The author explains that the earthly tabernacle was only a figure of the heavenly reality, and that Christ's superior sacrifice was necessary to purify the heavenly things themselves.

citation: Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith
paraphrase: The author urges believers to approach God with a sincere heart, full of faith, their hearts cleansed from guilt and their bodies washed with pure water.
contexte: The author of Hebrews encourages believers to approach God confidently through Jesus Christ, the high priest, as part of a series of exhortations.

citation: after that we have received the knowledge of the truth
paraphrase: After receiving the knowledge of the truth, if we deliberately persist in sin, no further sacrifice for sins remains.
contexte: The author warns believers not to abandon their assembly but to encourage one another, because willful sin after knowing the truth leaves no remaining sacrifice for sins.

citation: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth
paraphrase: God, by his own sovereign will, gave us new birth through the message of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of all his creatures.
contexte: James warns his beloved brethren not to err, affirming that every good and perfect gift comes from the unchanging Father of lights.

citation: and lie not against the truth
paraphrase: If you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition, do not boast about it or deny the truth by your actions.
contexte: James addresses believers who claim wisdom but harbor bitter envy and selfish ambition, warning them against boasting and lying against the truth.

citation: if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him
paraphrase: If any believer strays from the truth and someone brings him back, that person should know he has saved a soul from death and covered many sins.
contexte: After citing Elijah's prayer as an example of effective prayer, James addresses the community about restoring a brother who has wandered from the truth.

citation: Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit
paraphrase: Since you have purified your souls by obeying the truth through the Spirit, resulting in genuine brotherly love, make sure to love one another earnestly from a pure heart.
contexte: Peter exhorts believers, who have been born again through the living word of God, to love one another sincerely because they have purified their souls by obeying the truth through the Spirit.

citation: this is the true grace of God wherein ye stand
paraphrase: Peter writes briefly through Silvanus, a faithful brother, to encourage and testify that the grace of God in which they stand is genuine.
contexte: Peter concludes his letter, commending Silvanus and confirming the true grace of God in which the believers stand, after encouraging them to remain steadfast in suffering.

citation: established in the present truth
paraphrase: Peter says he will always remind his readers of these teachings, even though they already know them and are firmly grounded in the truth they presently have.
contexte: Peter, knowing his death is near, urges believers to remember the truths they already know so they remain firm in the faith.

citation: the way of truth shall be evil spoken of
paraphrase: Many will follow the destructive practices of false teachers, and because of them the true way of God will be slandered.
contexte: Peter warns that false teachers will arise and many will follow their destructive ways, causing the way of truth to be blasphemed.

citation: according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again
paraphrase: What happened to them illustrates the true proverb: a dog returns to its own vomit, and a washed sow returns to wallowing in the mire.
contexte: Peter describes the fate of those who, after knowing Christ, return to their former sins, comparing them to proverbs about dogs and pigs.

citation: we lie, and do not the truth
paraphrase: If we claim to have fellowship with God yet walk in darkness, we are lying and not living out the truth.
contexte: John, having proclaimed that God is light and in him is no darkness at all, now shows that claiming fellowship with God while walking in darkness is a lie.

citation: the truth is not in us
paraphrase: If we claim to be without sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.
contexte: John warns believers against self-deception, contrasting walking in darkness with walking in the light and confessing sins.

citation: and the truth is not in him
paraphrase: Anyone who claims to know God but does not obey his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in them.
contexte: John contrasts genuine knowledge of God, which is evidenced by obedience to his commandments, with the false claim of knowing him while disobeying.

citation: which thing is true in him and in you
paraphrase: John reiterates that he is writing a new commandment whose truth is evident both in Christ and in the believers, since the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.
contexte: John contrasts an old commandment with a new one, affirming that its truth is realized in Christ and in believers because darkness is passing and the true light is already shining.

citation: but because ye know it, and that no lie is of the truth
paraphrase: The author writes not because the readers lack knowledge of the truth, but because they possess it, and they recognize that no lie originates from the truth.
contexte: John addresses believers who have been warned about antichrists, emphasizing that they already know the truth through the Holy Spirit's anointing.

citation: But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him.
paraphrase: The anointing received from Christ remains in believers, so they do not need anyone to teach them; this same anointing teaches them about all things, is true and not a lie, and just as it has taught them, they will remain in Him.
contexte: John writes to believers to warn them about deceivers and to assure them that the Holy Spirit's anointing remains in them.

citation: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.
paraphrase: John encourages his dear children not to love merely with words or speech, but with actions and in truth.
contexte: John exhorts believers to show genuine love through actions and truth, not just words, following his teaching on self-sacrificial love and compassion for those in need.

citation: we know that we are of the truth
paraphrase: This is how we know that we belong to the truth and can set our hearts at rest in his presence.
contexte: After urging believers to love not just in words but in actions and truth, the author explains that this is how we can know we belong to the truth and reassure our hearts before God.

citation: Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.
paraphrase: Those who belong to God listen to us, while those who do not belong to God do not listen to us; this is how we distinguish the spirit of truth from the spirit of error.
contexte: In the context of distinguishing true and false spirits, John contrasts those who are of God and listen to the apostolic teaching with those who are of the world and do not listen.

citation: the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth
paraphrase: Jesus Christ is the one who came by water and blood, not by water only but by water and blood, and the Spirit bears witness to him because the Spirit is truth.
contexte: John explains that Jesus Christ came by water and blood, and that the Spirit bears witness to this because the Spirit is truth.

citation: that we may know him that is true
paraphrase: We know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the true God; we are in the true God through his Son Jesus Christ, who is the true God and eternal life.
contexte: The author assures believers of their knowledge of God through the coming of his Son, contrasting their secure position with the world's wickedness, and concludes with a warning against idols.

citation: The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth;
paraphrase: The elder greets the chosen lady and her children, loving them in the truth—a love shared by everyone who has come to know the truth.
contexte: The elder opens his second epistle by addressing an elect lady and her children, expressing love grounded in the truth that all believers share.

citation: For the truth’s sake, which dwelleth in us
paraphrase: C'est à cause de la vérité qui demeure en nous et qui sera avec nous pour toujours que l'auteur écrit à la dame élue et à ses enfants.
contexte: L'ancien s'adresse à la dame élue et à ses enfants, qu'il aime dans la vérité, et il leur souhaite la grâce, la miséricorde et la paix.

citation: Grace be with you, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
paraphrase: May you receive grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
contexte: The elder addresses the elect lady and her children, greeting them with grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Jesus Christ, in truth and love.

citation: I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth
paraphrase: John rejoices because he has found some of the lady's children living according to the truth, just as the Father commanded.
contexte: John writes to the elect lady and her children, expressing joy that some of them are living according to the truth.

citation: whom I love in the truth.
paraphrase: The elder greets his dear friend Gaius, affirming his sincere love for him grounded in the truth.
contexte: The elder addresses his beloved Gaius, expressing his love for him in the truth, before wishing him prosperity and health.

citation: the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth
paraphrase: I rejoiced greatly when the brethren came and testified to the truth that is in you, just as you walk in the truth.
contexte: John writes to Gaius, expressing joy because brethren testified that Gaius walks in the truth.

citation: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
contexte: John expresses his deep joy upon hearing from traveling brethren that Gaius continues to live faithfully in the truth.

citation: fellowhelpers to the truth
paraphrase: We should welcome and support such workers so that we become coworkers in spreading the truth.
contexte: John urges Gaius to welcome traveling missionaries who spread the gospel, in contrast to Diotrephes who refuses to receive them.

citation: and of the truth itself: yea, and we also bear record
paraphrase: Démétrius reçoit un bon témoignage de tous, et la vérité elle-même lui rend témoignage ; Jean et les autres confirment ce témoignage, que les destinataires savent véridique.
contexte: Après avoir mis en garde contre Diotrèphe qui rejette les frères, Jean recommande Démétrius, dont le témoignage est confirmé par tous et par la vérité elle-même.

citation: These things saith he that is holy, he that is true,
paraphrase: Jesus commands John to write to the angel of the church in Philadelphia, saying that He is holy and true, holds the key of David, and has absolute authority to open and shut doors that no one can reverse.
contexte: Jesus Christ instructs John to write to the angel of the church in Philadelphia, describing Himself as holy and true, with authority over opening and shutting.

citation: the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God;
paraphrase: Christ instructs John to write to the angel of the church in Laodicea, identifying himself as the Amen, the faithful and true witness, and the beginning of God's creation.
contexte: The risen Christ dictates a message to the church in Laodicea, introducing himself as the Amen and faithful witness before rebuking their lukewarmness.

citation: O Lord, holy and true
paraphrase: The martyred souls cry out loudly, asking the holy and true Lord how long until He judges and avenges their blood on the earth's inhabitants.
contexte: Under the fifth seal, the souls of martyrs slain for God's word cry out for divine judgment and vengeance.

citation: just and true are thy ways, thou King of saints.
paraphrase: Les rachetés chantent le cantique de Moïse et de l'Agneau, proclamant que les œuvres du Seigneur Dieu Tout-Puissant sont grandes et merveilleuses, et que ses voies sont justes et véritables, lui le Roi des saints.
contexte: Dans une vision céleste, Jean voit les vainqueurs de la bête se tenant sur une mer de verre et chantant le cantique de Moïse et de l'Agneau.

citation: true and righteous are thy judgments
paraphrase: A voice from the altar affirms that the judgments of the Lord God Almighty are true and righteous.
contexte: After the angel of the waters declares God's judgments righteous because the wicked shed the blood of saints and prophets, another voice from the altar confirms that God's judgments are true and righteous.

citation: For true and righteous are his judgments
paraphrase: God's judgments are true and righteous because He has judged the great whore who corrupted the earth and has avenged the blood of His servants.
contexte: A great multitude in heaven praises God for His true and righteous judgments against the great whore who corrupted the earth.

citation: These are the true sayings of God.
paraphrase: The angel tells John to write that those invited to the Lamb's marriage supper are blessed, and confirms that these words are God's true sayings.
contexte: An angel instructs John to write about the blessedness of those called to the marriage supper of the Lamb, affirming the truth of God's words.

citation: he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True
paraphrase: Jean voit le ciel ouvert et un cheval blanc dont le cavalier s'appelle Fidèle et Vrai, et qui juge et fait la guerre avec justice.
contexte: Après que l'ange lui a interdit de l'adorer et a rendu témoignage de Jésus, Jean voit le ciel s'ouvrir et un cavalier monté sur un cheval blanc.

citation: for these words are true and faithful
paraphrase: The one seated on the throne declares that He is making all things new and instructs John to write, because these words are true and faithful.
contexte: After describing the new heaven and new earth where God dwells with humanity and wipes away every tear, the one seated on the throne declares He is making all things new and commands John to write.

citation: These sayings are faithful and true
paraphrase: The angel tells John that these prophetic words are trustworthy and true, and that the Lord God, who inspired the prophets, sent his angel to reveal to his servants what must soon take place.
contexte: An angel speaks to John after showing him the vision of the new Jerusalem, affirming the trustworthiness of the prophetic sayings.
